summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend testing of AMASS Admin Portal. Backend: 31 pytest tests covering auth, dashboard, leads CRUD/filter/CSV, CMS section update+public reflection, visibility toggle, roles matrix, RBAC (content_manager, finance, super_admin), team management. All 31 passed. Frontend: Playwright tested login (valid+invalid), dashboard (7 stat cards render with data, leads trend, lead-sources pie, activities), nav to Leads/CMS/Roles/Settings, lead view dialog, type filter, CMS save (toast confirmed), roles page (84 perm checkboxes visible for marketing role), super_admin locked, settings tabs (profile/security/team), theme toggle (light->dark), placeholder module coming-soon. All flows working.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 719 lines — approaching the >700 threshold. Consider splitting into routers (auth, leads, cms, roles, dashboard, seed) for maintainability.

CORS is set to allow_origins='*' with allow_credentials=True. Browsers reject this combination for cookie-based auth; since app falls back to Bearer token from localStorage it currently works, but this is a latent auth-hardening issue. Set explicit origins if enabling cookie flow.

get_current_user reads token from cookie 'access_token' but frontend stores token as 'amass_token' in localStorage and sends only via Authorization header. Cookie path in login response sets HttpOnly cookie but frontend never relies on it — cookie flow is essentially dead code; either fully wire it (fetch with credentials:'include') or drop it to reduce surprise.
Recharts warnings 'width(-1) height(-1)' during initial render — cosmetic, resolves on layout.
Storing raw JWT in localStorage (amass_token) is vulnerable to XSS; since HttpOnly cookie is already set on login, consider migrating fully to cookie-based auth.
